text:
Naomi Feldman: hey folks — quick review request on the audit logging one-pager. want to make sure we’re not overstating what’s logged / how exports work.

Draft in Drive: https://drive.google.com/.../audit-logging-overview-one-pager (same content will go to Confluence)

2 things I need Security Eng eyes on:
1) “What’s logged today” section (event types + any exclusions)
2) Export mechanisms + any roadmap disclaimers (don’t want to promise native SIEM push if not GA)

Kevin Osei: thanks. skimmed. couple corrections/precision items.

What we ACTUALLY log today (Console Audit Logs):
- org/project admin actions: create/delete project, rename, settings changes
- API credentials: create/revoke key, rotate key (shows actor + target)
- identity/access: role granted/revoked, user invited/removed, permission changes
- auth config changes: SSO/SAML enable/disable + config updates (NOT the raw SAML assertions)
- model serving ops (control-plane): model enabled/disabled for a project, rollout policy changes (canary/traffic split), endpoint config changes

What we do NOT log (and shouldn’t imply):
- individual inference request payloads/prompts/responses
- customer data in request bodies
- “every console page view” / general clickstream

Also: keep language as “audit logs capture administrative and configuration actions in the Redwood control plane” vs “all actions”.

Marcus Lin: +1 to Kevin. also please avoid “immutable” unless we’re specifying the storage guarantees.

We can say “audit logs are append-only within Redwood’s logging pipeline; entries include timestamp, actor identity, source IP (where available), action, and target resource.”

But if we say “tamper-proof” we’ll get dragged into details.

Naomi Feldman: got it. I’ll remove “tamper-proof/immutable”.

On export — draft currently says:
- “download CSV/JSON”
- “export to SIEM via webhook”

Is webhook true today?

Kevin Osei: webhook is NOT generally available.

Current export options (as of now):
- manual export from Console (CSV or JSONL)
- Audit Logs API (pull) for enterprise tenants (used by customers to ingest into Splunk/Sentinel/Datadog etc)

We’ve done one-off S3 delivery / scheduled exports for specific enterprise deals, but that’s not self-serve. I’d mark that as “available on request” only if we’re comfortable w/ support burden.

Roadmap: native push integrations (webhook / SIEM connectors) being explored but not committed.

Ethan Park: on “source IP where available” — yes for console/admin actions (user session) we capture IP. for API key actions coming from automation, we capture client IP from the request if not behind weird proxies.

But we shouldn’t promise “always includes IP” because of NAT/proxy scenarios.

Suggested wording: “may include source IP and user agent, depending on request context.”

Elliot Price: for Docs / external wording: can we also clearly separate Hosted/Dedicated/Private?

I worry the draft currently reads like the same export options exist everywhere.

Kira Thompson: +1 — I’m editing the Dedicated/Private variants and could use exact boundary language.

Kevin Osei: boundary notes:

Hosted + Dedicated:
- audit logs cover Redwood Console + control plane actions for the tenant
- export via Console + API as above

Private (VPC/on-prem):
- audit logs still cover control plane actions (org/admin/config) IF customer is using Redwood control plane
- runtime logs (cluster/system logs, request logs at the inference layer) live in customer environment and are customer-managed
- export mechanisms depend on customer infra; we can provide schemas + recommended patterns, but we’re not operating their SIEM pipeline

Avoid saying “we export audit logs from Private to your SIEM” as a blanket statement.

Marcus Lin: also on “what is logged” — please add a line like:
“Audit logs are designed for security/compliance auditing of administrative actions, not for application-level observability.”

This helps with the recurring “do you log all prompts?” question.

Naomi Feldman: makes sense.

One more nit: the draft has “retention: 1 year by default”. I think that’s wrong / varies?

Kevin Osei: yeah, varies by plan + deployment mode. Don’t hardcode a number.

Better:
- “Audit logs are retained for a default period based on your plan; extended retention may be available for enterprise.”
- and then point to the retention one-pager for specifics.

If we need a safe statement: “minimum 30 days” might still be contentious. I’d keep it qualitative unless GRC insists.

Elliot Price: +1 keep it qualitative and link to retention doc. Otherwise we’ll break it every time packaging changes.

Naomi Feldman: ok. I’ll update:
- remove webhook/SIEM push claim
- tighten event list + add “not prompts/responses” callout
- adjust Hosted/Dedicated/Private boundaries
- remove hard retention number; refer to retention controls one-pager

I’ll repost the revised text here for final thumbs.

---

Naomi Feldman: Revision v3 pasted (for quick review):

“Redwood Audit Logs record administrative and configuration actions in the Redwood control plane (e.g., user/role changes, API credential lifecycle events, and key project/endpoint configuration updates). Audit logs are intended for security/compliance auditing and do not include customer inference request payloads (prompts, inputs, or model outputs).

Export: Audit logs can be viewed in the Console and exported via manual download (CSV/JSONL). For eligible enterprise plans, audit logs may also be accessed via API to support ingestion into customer logging/SIEM tooling. Additional export options may be available on request.

Deployment modes: Hosted and Dedicated include audit logs for your tenant’s control plane actions. In Private deployments, control plane audit logs cover administrative actions, while runtime/system logs for customer-managed infrastructure are owned and operated by the customer.”

Thoughts?

Kevin Osei: looks good. One tweak: “eligible enterprise plans” -> “enterprise plans” (less wiggle) and “may also be accessed via API” -> “can be accessed via API” if that’s actually enabled for enterprise tiers consistently.

Also “additional export options may be available on request” is fine.

Marcus Lin: approved with Kevin’s wording tweaks. :thumbsup:

Ethan Park: approved. :thumbsup: also +1 to keeping IP language out of the one-pager.

Elliot Price: good from docs side. once you update the canonical Confluence page, ping me and I’ll make sure the docs-site snippet doesn’t drift.

Kira Thompson: :thumbsup: I’ll align the Private boundary section in the RFP library with this language.

Naomi Feldman: awesome — I’ll incorporate tweaks + move to Confluence for final review stamp today.
